GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Senior TA Operations Specialist, you’ll own the dashboards and recurring reporting that recruiters and leaders use to make hiring decisions at GitLab. You’ll define how Talent Acquisition (TA) measures hiring, use artificial intelligence (AI) to automate reporting work, and turn findings into recommendations. You’ll also own the systems recruiters rely on and lead operations initiatives from defining the problem through rollout, adoption, and measurement.

What You’ll Do  

  • Own TA dashboards, from defining recruiting metrics to building and maintaining reports. Check that the same metrics use consistent definitions and match across dashboards and recurring reports.
  • Deliver recurring reports for recruiters, TA leaders, and executives on pipeline health, conversion between hiring stages, time to hire, sourcing effectiveness, and progress against the hiring plan. Recommend changes and track which recommendations lead to action.
  • Use AI to automate data preparation, flag unusual changes, and draft written analysis so reports explain the numbers. Track the time it takes to prepare each recurring report to see whether automation saves time.
  • Lead TA Operations initiatives from business case and stakeholder agreement through design, build, and rollout. Define success before launch, track adoption and results, and revise or retire solutions that don’t deliver.
  • Configure GitLab’s recruiting tools, including hiring stages, fields, picklists, scorecards, user access, and permissions in the applicant tracking system (ATS). Own the integrations, lead incident response, and track failures and time to restore service.
  • Build and deploy AI agents and automated workflows for recruiting and reporting. Refine prompts, manage models, and track how often agents complete the tasks they’re designed to handle.
  • Build business cases for investing in AI and reporting tools using adoption data. Track usage after rollout to see whether the tools are being adopted as expected.
  • Own TA’s AI governance framework. Track which AI workflows have completed bias audits, fairness reviews, and privacy compliance checks.

What You’ll Bring 

  • Experience in recruiting operations, human resources technology, or a related field.
  • Experience building and owning recruiting dashboards for senior stakeholders.
  • Ability to extract, validate, and visualize data, then explain what it means for hiring decisions.
  • Experience using AI to speed up reporting and analysis.
  • A track record of leading initiatives from problem definition to launch and adoption.
  • Experience configuring and owning an enterprise ATS and its integrations.
  • Hands-on experience building and deploying AI agents or automated workflows.

We welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience. Many successful candidates don’t meet every requirement.

About the team

In Talent Acquisition Operations, we support the systems, reporting, and workflows GitLab uses to hire. You’ll work with our recruiters, TA leaders, and executives to make hiring data easier to act on and bring automation into recruiting workflows with clear standards for fairness and privacy. We work remotely and asynchronously.

The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity. Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary.

United States Salary Range
$104,800—$176,400 USD

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

  • Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
  • Flexible Paid Time Off 
  • Team Member Resource Groups
  • Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Growth and Development Fund
  • Parental Leave 

Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.

Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.
